title: A toric Calabi-Yau counterexample to Schimpf's connected stable pairs pole conjecture
summary: Schimpf's connected reformulation of Pandharipande's pole conjecture for stable pairs predicts the following restriction: in class \(β\), connected descendent coefficients have nonzero \(p\)-poles only where \(-p\) is an \(m\)-th root of unity with \(1\leq m\leq\divis(β)\). We give a toric counterexample. The threefold is a smooth quasi-projective toric Calabi--Yau threefold whose compact torus-invariant curves form a chain \(C_1\cup C_2\).
